newsitem.title: USA: Armstrong says committed to Domco bid.
newsitem.headline: Armstrong says committed to Domco bid.

text.p: Armstrong World Industries Inc said Wednesday it is committed to its two-month, C$23 per share hostile bid for Canadian flooring manufactuer Domco Inc.
Yesterday, Domco's board rejected Armstrong's offer and decided it will not issue new shares as proposed under Armstrong's modified takeover proposal.
Domco is 57 percent owned by France's Sommer Allibert, on a fully diluted basis.
Sommer, which in the spring entered a complicated deal to combine its flooring business with that of Germany's Tarkett AG, does not back the Armstrong offer.
An Armstrong spokeswoman, reading from a prepared statement, said: "Domco's board has placed the desires and interests of Sommer Allibert over those of its other shareholders and constituencies.

"Although we have not seen the board's offical circular that will be mailed to shareholders, we note that the board's press release provides no rationale for their action other than the stated intentions of Sommer Alliber."

The spokeswoman pointed out that Domco's board "did not say that our offering price was inadequate. The board's rejection of our proposal is in effect an endorsement of the Sommer-Tarkett transaction, which provides no immediate value to Domco shareholders. Our offer of C$23 is the only equal treatment solution."
Armstrong, based in Lancaster, Pa., is seeking an injunction in U.S. federal court to block the Sommer-Tarkett transaction, valued at about $565 million.
The total value of the Armstrong Domco bid is about C$488 million.

Armstrong modified its bid for Farnham, Quebec-based Domco on July 3, making the offer conditional on receiving 51 percent of all shares being tendered on a fully diluted basis. The offer was due to expire on August 15, 1997.

In its modified offer, Armstrong proposed to subscribe at C$23 a share for a number of newly issued shares, which together with the Domco securities tendered under the offer, would give it 51 percent of Domco shares on a fully diluted basis.
